After trying this for some time, I am convinced it is not possible unless you bruteforce the form. The only thing I found that was of note is that the action/password page (the page that handles all password submissions to join rooms) can be used for rooms that have no passwords set. It will even give you a unique access key on your url like the one given when you join a password protected room, though it is not actually submitted because I was still able to join an unprotected room with @pembo210's key.

If anyone wants to try and get into the room, here is some info:

  • http://voat.co/signalr/hubs here is a list of the websocket functions that chat uses.

This is what a request to send a message in chat looks like:

{"H":"messaginghub","M":"SendChatMessage","A":["whatever","REEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE test",""],"I":0}

You could send messages to another room by changing the room name from "whatever" to something else, but it will not work with password protected rooms. Here is an example of a message sent to a password protected room:

{"H":"messaginghub","M":"SendChatMessage","A":["passphrase","test","4nqYN+CjqtAyDAA9p9GjRQ=="],"I":0}

Note that there is another field there now. It is the same unique string that is put on the end of a room url when a password is given, so you will not be able to send messages to rooms you don't have a correct string for.

  • To access a password protected room, you will need to send a valid request verification token, a room ID and a password. Request tokens are all unique, and are not tied to accounts, similar to the tokens submitted when you make a post or comment. Bad passwords sent in requests still give a unique room string in the response. Request example:

__RequestVerificationToken=0IZtbTpPnN3iX3FX4e3Ht7ff5pADUCv2syu_PHWDmR8HDfA9hXzs4YzW4FXgYv4EnaEZmZGjk8UJ8F29UQG6Rp2LnquxM5oi1YQEC8vSMpf9THEbz0rgS3Zi54zFJAr8wARYWaz5di6l4_IStF_f1g2&room.ID=hack&room.Passphrase=jetfuelcantmeltsteelbeams

When I submit this request, I get a response with a key in it:

<html><head><title>Object moved</title></head><body>

<h2>Object moved to <a href="/chat/hack?access=S245t%2BUHptB6yvGDw9mAWw%3D%3D">here</a>.</h2>

</body></html>

But it is a bad key, so I am redirected back to the password form.

  • The %3D%3D at the end of the unique string can be changed to "==" and it will still work. However, if you get a %2B in the middle of a key, and change it to +, it will not work. For some reason.

  • Secret rooms are secret and unique strings can not be found by crawling through site pages.

That is basically it. If you want the password, blackmail Putt into giving it to you or bruteforce the form.
